claims.text: The fact this case turns on — when the driver arrived — is carried only by evidence the pre-pass has already impaired. The trip record's own event reads 'Driver GPS within 10m of pickup point. Speed 0 km/h. Auto-arrival confirmed.', i.e. the arrival marker was generated from the GPS fix itself, so under POL-GEN-02 the marker and the trace are one carrier rather than two and the 'corroboration' is the platform checking the fix against the fix. That single carrier runs at weight 0.6, and the pre-pass names the issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD, with only four fixes inside the waiting window against the six the gap rule requires. POL-GEN-26 lists 'when the driver arrived' as one of the facts that must be escalated, not decided, where the evidence carrying it is missing or impaired, and it forbids an outcome being inferred from that impaired record. The 5.00 SGD should therefore be held for a human reviewer rather than collected from the rider.

Even if the arrival marker is taken at face value, no final AI ruling can issue on this record at the confidence POL-GEN-22 demands. The rider's profile carries fraud_flags = 1, and POL-GEN-22 fixes the required confidence at 0.95 whatever the value of the dispute — the 'final at any confidence' band does not survive a fraud flag. POL-GEN-02(2) forbids confidence above the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding facts: the fee charged is carried by EV-FARE-00903, which is marked PARTIAL_RECORD at weight 0.75, and the arrival by EV-GPS-00903, marked LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD at weight 0.6. The ceiling is 0.6, far short of 0.95, so the case goes to human review under POL-GEN-26 — which holds the charge rather than collecting it, and is the outcome that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed 5.00 SGD.

The rider's account — that they were at the pickup — is tested by nothing in the record, and nothing in the record can fill the gap. The trace carries no rider track at all: rider_track is empty, and the pre-pass records that the rider-track limb is engaged precisely because no rider track was supplied. The trace is therefore impaired on both parties' presence, at weight 0.6 with issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD. POL-GEN-26 provides that no outcome may be inferred from the absence of evidence except where a rule says so, and no no-show clause makes rider absence provable by default; a no-show finding against the rider here would rest on the very inference that clause forbids. The open question belongs to a human reviewer, with the fee held.

claims.text: The driver was at the pickup before the scheduled time. trip_record.arrived_at is 08:43:00, two minutes ahead of the 08:45:00 scheduled pickup, and the record's own driver_deadline check returns arrived_by_deadline true against the 08:50:00 deadline. The category's arrival test is met: the nearest GPS fix sits at distance 0.0 m from the pickup point at 08:43:00, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the code-computed arrival check returns corroborated true. POL-NS-21's arrival test uses that fix at its reported position, because the 25 m accuracy filter applies only to a fix that reports an accuracy and this one reports none. I disclose that the GPS trace is impaired (weight 0.6; issues LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD): the impairment goes to the trace's sparse 180 s sampling, not to the single stationary fix standing at the pickup, and the candidate explanation that the arrival marker and the trace are 'one carrier' does not survive the policy's own arrival test, which contemplates a trip-record marker corroborated by a GPS fix and tells us how to treat a fix with no reported accuracy.

The free wait was served. Because the driver arrived at 08:43:00, before the 08:45:00 scheduled pickup, POL-NS-21 fixes the free wait from trip_record.scheduled_at rather than from arrival, so the 300 s free wait ran from 08:45:00 to 08:50:00. The driver cancelled at 08:51:00, after it expired, and the record's free_wait check returns cancelled_after_free_wait true with seconds_from_start_to_cancel 360.0.

POL-NS-23's contact obligation is satisfied, so the FULL_REFUND that clause licenses is not triggered. Before cancelling at 08:51:00 the driver sent four in-app messages at 08:43:00, 08:45:20, 08:49:30 and 08:50:45, and placed one in-app call at 08:47:05 that rang 22 s unanswered. Both limbs the clause requires are therefore present on trip_record.in_app_calls and in the chat log, all before cancelled_at, and the code-computed contact_before_cancel check returns obligation_met true.

POL-NS-24's route to a full refund is not open on this record. That clause operates only where the driver fails to reach the pickup by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes - here 08:45:00 + 5 min = 08:50:00 - and the driver arrived at 08:43:00, seven minutes inside the deadline, with arrived_by_deadline returning true. Nor was contact un-attempted, so the clause's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise either.

The fee charged is exactly the fee in force, and it stands. The fare ledger records a single 5.00 SGD cancellation fee with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, and its money block returns fee_matches_policy true against POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD fee. Every no-show condition holds - arrival, the served free wait, and the contact obligation - so the rider's claim fails, the present charge stands, and POL-NS-22 directs the ruling DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00. I disclose that the fare ledger is impaired (weight 0.75; issue PARTIAL_RECORD): the one line it carries reconciles exactly with the fee in force, so no overcharge or shortfall is in issue and the fee-amount check produces no referral.

The rider's account that they waited at the lobby is carried by nothing in the record. The GPS trace's rider_track is empty, so no rider fix places the rider at the pickup at any point in the waiting window; I disclose that the trace itself is impaired (weight 0.6; issues LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD), but its rider_track is empty rather than merely sparse, so no rider presence is recorded at all. The chat log, which is complete at weight 1.0, holds no rider message across the driver's four messages between 08:43:00 and 08:50:45. The filer's untested assertion is the only support for the claim, against driver-side evidence of arrival, wait and contact that stands unrebutted, so the no-show the driver acted on is the only state the record shows.

No fact this case needs is left unestablished, so POL-GEN-26 does not arise and POL-NS-26 leaves the no-show ruling with the AI. The facts that decide it - arrival, the served free wait and the contact obligation - rest on EV-TRIP-00903 and EV-CHAT-00903, both complete artifacts at weight 1.0; the GPS trace (0.6; LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD) and the fare ledger (0.75; PARTIAL_RECORD) corroborate and record those facts rather than carry them alone, and I disclose their impairment rather than build the ruling on it. There is accordingly no open question for a reviewer to resolve and no ground to hold the fee.

ruling.explanation:
Rider R-7823 and driver D-2398 — this decides the 5.00 SGD no-show fee on TRIP-2026-09945.

What the record shows. The driver's arrival marker is 08:43:00 on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00903), two minutes before the 08:45:00 scheduled pickup. Because he arrived before the scheduled time, POL-NS-21 runs the 300 s free wait from the scheduled time, 08:45:00 to 08:50:00, and he cancelled at 08:51:00, after it expired. POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met: before cancelling he sent four in-app messages (08:43:00, 08:45:20, 08:49:30, 08:50:45) and placed one in-app call at 08:47:05 that rang 22 s unanswered — both limbs present before cancelled_at. POL-NS-24 does not refund the fee: it opens only if the driver failed to reach the pickup by 08:50:00, and he arrived at 08:43:00. The amount charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so POL-NS-22 makes the fee stand: DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

The rider's arguments, and why they do not change the result. (a) The rider says the arrival rests only on impaired evidence and that the trip record's auto-arrival marker and the GPS trace are one carrier. I accept that: the marker was generated from the GPS measurement, so the two do not corroborate each other, and the trace is impaired (EV-GPS-00903, weight 0.6; LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD). But the arrival is independently carried by the driver's contemporaneous chat, sent from inside the disputed window (EV-CHAT-00903, weight 1.0, COMPLETE) — 'I've arrived at the pickup point, I'm at the lobby area' at 08:43:00 and 'I'm waiting at the lobby area…' at 08:45:20. Remove the instruments and those messages still support the finding, so the chat is an independent carrier, not a restatement; under POL-GEN-02(2) the cap takes the higher of two independent carriers of the same fact, 1.0 rather than 0.6. (b) The rider is right that the fraud flag on the profile raises the required confidence to 0.95 (POL-GEN-22, and POL-NS-26 for no-shows), but wrong that the ceiling is 0.6: the deciding facts — arrival (chat, 1.0), the free wait and the contact obligation (EV-TRIP-00903, 1.0, and chat, 1.0) and the 5.00 fee (trip record and EV-FARE-00903) — are carried by complete artifacts, so 1.0 is permitted and the 0.95 bar is met. (c) The rider is right that the trace carries no rider track, but no clause in this category makes proof of the rider's presence a condition of the fee; POL-NS-21 and POL-NS-23 test the driver's wait and the driver's contact, and POL-NS-24 tests only his arrival. POL-GEN-26 is therefore not engaged — when the driver arrived is established.

Impairment disclosed. The ruling does not rest on the impaired artifacts: EV-GPS-00903 (0.6; LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD) and EV-FARE-00903 (0.75; PARTIAL_RECORD) corroborate only, and EV-ADVIS-00903-01 is absent (0.0) and carries no fact.

Referrals: none. A fee of exactly 5.00 SGD produces no POL-NS-22 referral; the driver attempted contact, so POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise; and the POL-NS-25 repeat no-show counter is not present on the rider's profile, so no flag issues.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee is neither confirmed against the rider nor refunded to them. The amount is held for a human reviewer.

What the record does establish. The cancellation came at 08:51:00 with a 5.00 SGD fee charged (EV-FARE-00903, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0) — the exact fee POL-NS-22 fixes, so the fee-amount check raises nothing. The free wait was served: the trip was scheduled for 08:45:00 and the driver arrived before it, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s wait ran 08:45:00–08:50:00 and the 08:51:00 cancellation fell after it (EV-TRIP-00903 free_wait check true). The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 was met: four in-app messages (08:43:00, 08:45:20, 08:49:30, 08:50:45) and one in-app call at 08:47:05 ringing 22 s unanswered, all before cancelled_at (EV-TRIP-00903, EV-CHAT-00903). The rider's account — that they were at the lobby and the driver never came — is carried by nothing: the GPS rider_track is empty and the chat log holds no rider message. So POL-NS-24's full-refund route is not open either, and its 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise because contact was attempted.

What the record cannot do. The case turns on the driver's arrival, and the only thing placing the driver at the pickup is a GPS measurement. The trip record's 08:43:00 arrival marker was auto-confirmed from that same fix (EV-TRIP-00903 event detail), so under POL-GEN-02 the marker and EV-GPS-00903 are one carrier, not two. That carrier is impaired: EV-GPS-00903 weighs 0.6 with issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD. EV-TRIP-00903 (1.0), EV-CHAT-00903 (1.0) and EV-FARE-00903 (0.75) do not lift it — the driver's own chat messages are his own assertions, not an independent measurement, and the fare ledger only records the fee. Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence on that fact cannot exceed 0.6.

The rider's profile carries fraud_flags = 1, so POL-GEN-22 requires a confidence of 0.95 for any AI ruling here whatever the 5.00 SGD value, and POL-NS-26 makes a no-show ruling final only subject to that 0.95. A ceiling of 0.6 cannot reach 0.95, and POL-GEN-26 names 'when the driver arrived' as a fact that must go to a human reviewer when the evidence carrying it is impaired. I therefore cannot confirm the 5.00 SGD fee against the rider, and equally cannot find for the rider that the driver never came. The driver's request for DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD fails on this bar, not on the merits; the rider's request that the charge be reversed fails for the same reason.

No referral arises: the POL-NS-24 goodwill credit does not fire (contact was attempted), the POL-NS-25 repeat no-show counter is not present on the rider profile, and the charge is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes, so no fee-amount referral under POL-NS-22. Open question for the reviewer: can the driver's auto-confirmed 08:43:00 arrival, and the rider's claimed presence, be resolved when no fix on the trace reports a horizontal accuracy?

This case goes to a human reviewer, and the disputed 5.00 SGD no-show fee is held — not collected from you (the rider) and not paid to the driver — until that review. Neither side gets a money outcome from me.

Why it cannot be decided at the standard this case requires. The driver's account is that he reached Tiong Bahru Plaza at 08:43, waited, sent four in-app messages and placed one in-app call, and cancelled after the free wait ran out at 08:50. If that is right, POL-NS-21 (free wait, run from the 08:45 schedule because he arrived early, expiring 08:50) and POL-NS-23 (contact obligation, satisfied by the 08:43/08:45:20/08:49:30/08:50:45 messages and the 08:47:05 call, all before the 08:51 cancellation — v2.1 2.3) are met and the fee stands under POL-NS-22, which would make the outcome DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD. Your account is that you were at the lobby and the car never came; the record does not independently prove otherwise, because the GPS trace's rider_track is empty and the chat log contains no message from you.

The record cannot settle which is right to the confidence this case needs, because of how the evidence is weighted. The only thing placing the driver at the pickup is the arrival measurement, and the pre-pass records that the trip record's 'driver_arrived' marker was auto-confirmed from the very same GPS fix, so the trip-record marker and the GPS trace are one carrier, not two independent ones; they cannot corroborate each other. That carrier is impaired: EV-GPS-00903 is marked LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD at weight 0.6 (180 s gaps inside the waiting window, only four fixes there against the six the gap rule wants, and no rider track at all). The money evidence is impaired too: EV-FARE-00903 is PARTIAL_RECORD at weight 0.75. Under POL-GEN-02(2) a ruling's confidence is capped at the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding facts, and because the arrival carrier is not independent of the clean trip record, the cap is 0.6, not the 1.0 the clean artifacts would suggest.

Your profile carries fraud_flags = 1. POL-GEN-22 therefore fixes the confidence an AI ruling needs at 0.95 whatever the value of the dispute (a 5.00 SGD case that would otherwise be AI-final at any confidence), and POL-NS-26 applies that bar to a no-show. The evidence caps confidence at 0.6, far short of 0.95, so no AI ruling — for you or against you — can issue on this record. Independently, POL-GEN-26 (the conservative reading of v2.1 6.3) says that where a fact a rule needs — here 'when the driver arrived', and whether you were present — cannot be established because the evidence carrying it is missing or impaired, the case is escalated and the open question stated. That open question is: did the driver actually reach the pickup and wait, or was the arrival marker an artefact of a sparse, auto-confirmed fix?

On the advocates' claims: the driver's claims that the arrival test is corroborated (POL-NS-21), that the free wait was served, and that the contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met (trip record and chat log, both weight 1.0) are supported for those limbs, but the driver's further claim that the deciding facts rest on clean 1.0 evidence is rejected — the arrival marker is one carrier with the impaired GPS trace (0.6), so it does not lift the cap. Your claims that the arrival fact is carried by impaired evidence, that the 0.95 bar cannot be met, and that your own presence is untested (empty rider track), are accepted, and they are why the fee is held. ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this no-show charge cannot be finally decided by the AI on the present record, so it goes to a human reviewer. The disputed 5.00 SGD cancellation fee is held — it is neither refunded to the rider nor released to the driver — until that review.

What the record shows. The rider was charged a 5.00 SGD cancellation fee (EV-FARE-00903) after driver D-2398 marked arrival at 08:43:00 and cancelled at 08:51:00 (EV-TRIP-00903). The scheduled pickup was 08:45:00. Because the driver arrived before the scheduled time, POL-NS-21 fixes the 300 s free wait from the scheduled time, i.e. 08:45:00 to 08:50:00; the cancellation at 08:51:00 came after it (EV-TRIP-00903, free_wait check cancelled_after_free_wait true, seconds_from_start_to_cancel 360.0). Before cancelling, the driver sent four in-app messages (08:43:00, 08:45:20, 08:49:30, 08:50:45) and placed one in-app call at 08:47:05 that rang 22 s unanswered (EV-CHAT-00903, EV-TRIP-00903), so POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met. The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD fee in force (EV-FARE-00903, fee_matches_policy true). POL-NS-24 gives no route to a refund: the driver arrived at 08:43:00, seven minutes inside the 08:50:00 deadline (arrived_by_deadline true), and contacted the rider, so neither the full refund nor the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit arises. On those facts the driver's side (claims that arrival is met, the free wait served, the contact obligation satisfied, POL-NS-24 closed, and the fee equal to the fee in force) is accepted.

Why the AI still cannot rule. The fact this case turns on — whether the driver was actually at the pickup — rests on the GPS trace EV-GPS-00903, which is impaired at weight 0.6 (issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD): its sampling gaps inside the waiting window exceed the 120 s policy threshold. The trip record's own arrival marker was auto-generated from that same GPS measurement ('Auto-arrival confirmed', EV-TRIP-00903), so under POL-GEN-02 the marker and the trace are one carrier, not two, and the trace's 0.6 is the ceiling for the arrival fact. The fare ledger EV-FARE-00903 is also impaired at 0.75 (PARTIAL_RECORD). The driver's submission that the deciding facts rest on EV-TRIP-00903 and EV-CHAT-00903 at weight 1.0 is accepted for the free-wait and contact facts but rejected for arrival: the marker merely restates the impaired GPS measurement and does not lift the cap. The rider's submission that the rider's own presence is untested (the trace's rider_track is empty and the chat log holds no rider message) is noted and is a further open question for the reviewer.

Under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence cannot exceed 0.6, and because the rider's profile carries a fraud flag of 1 (EV-RPROF-00903), POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 require a confidence of 0.95 whatever the dispute value. The record cannot reach that bar, so the ruling is ESCALATE and the amount is held; no monetary outcome issues.

No referral arises. The fee charged is exactly 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount check produces none; POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not apply because the driver both arrived by the deadline and attempted contact; and POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag does not apply because the rider profile carries no no-show counter (the field is absent, and POL-NS-25 acts only when it is present).

ledger.claim: The fact this case turns on — when the driver arrived — is carried only by evidence the pre-pass has already impaired. The trip record's own event reads 'Driver GPS within 10m of pickup point. Speed 0 km/h. Auto-arrival confirmed.', i.e. the arrival marker was generated from the GPS fix itself, so under POL-GEN-02 the marker and the trace are one carrier rather than two and the 'corroboration' is the platform checking the fix against the fix. That single carrier runs at weight 0.6, and the pre-pass names the issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD, with only four fixes inside the waiting window against the six the gap rule requires. POL-GEN-26 lists 'when the driver arrived' as one of the facts that must be escalated, not decided, where the evidence carrying it is missing or impaired, and it forbids an outcome being inferred from that impaired record. The 5.00 SGD should therefore be held for a human reviewer rather than collected from the rider.

Even if the arrival marker is taken at face value, no final AI ruling can issue on this record at the confidence POL-GEN-22 demands. The rider's profile carries fraud_flags = 1, and POL-GEN-22 fixes the required confidence at 0.95 whatever the value of the dispute — the 'final at any confidence' band does not survive a fraud flag. POL-GEN-02(2) forbids confidence above the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding facts: the fee charged is carried by EV-FARE-00903, which is marked PARTIAL_RECORD at weight 0.75, and the arrival by EV-GPS-00903, marked LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD at weight 0.6. The ceiling is 0.6, far short of 0.95, so the case goes to human review under POL-GEN-26 — which holds the charge rather than collecting it, and is the outcome that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed 5.00 SGD.

The rider's account — that they were at the pickup — is tested by nothing in the record, and nothing in the record can fill the gap. The trace carries no rider track at all: rider_track is empty, and the pre-pass records that the rider-track limb is engaged precisely because no rider track was supplied. The trace is therefore impaired on both parties' presence, at weight 0.6 with issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD. POL-GEN-26 provides that no outcome may be inferred from the absence of evidence except where a rule says so, and no no-show clause makes rider absence provable by default; a no-show finding against the rider here would rest on the very inference that clause forbids. The open question belongs to a human reviewer, with the fee held.

The driver was at the pickup before the scheduled time. trip_record.arrived_at is 08:43:00, two minutes ahead of the 08:45:00 scheduled pickup, and the record's own driver_deadline check returns arrived_by_deadline true against the 08:50:00 deadline. The category's arrival test is met: the nearest GPS fix sits at distance 0.0 m from the pickup point at 08:43:00, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the code-computed arrival check returns corroborated true. POL-NS-21's arrival test uses that fix at its reported position, because the 25 m accuracy filter applies only to a fix that reports an accuracy and this one reports none. I disclose that the GPS trace is impaired (weight 0.6; issues LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD): the impairment goes to the trace's sparse 180 s sampling, not to the single stationary fix standing at the pickup, and the candidate explanation that the arrival marker and the trace are 'one carrier' does not survive the policy's own arrival test, which contemplates a trip-record marker corroborated by a GPS fix and tells us how to treat a fix with no reported accuracy.

The free wait was served. POL-NS-24's route to a full refund is not open on this record. Nor was contact un-attempted, so the clause's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise either.

The fee charged is exactly the fee in force, and it stands. The fare ledger records a single 5.00 SGD cancellation fee with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, and its money block returns fee_matches_policy true against POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD fee. Every no-show condition holds - arrival, the served free wait, and the contact obligation - so the rider's claim fails, the present charge stands, and POL-NS-22 directs the ruling DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00. I disclose that the fare ledger is impaired (weight 0.75; issue PARTIAL_RECORD): the one line it carries reconciles exactly with the fee in force, so no overcharge or shortfall is in issue and the fee-amount check produces no referral.

The rider's account that they waited at the lobby is carried by nothing in the record. The GPS trace's rider_track is empty, so no rider fix places the rider at the pickup at any point in the waiting window; I disclose that the trace itself is impaired (weight 0.6; issues LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD), but its rider_track is empty rather than merely sparse, so no rider presence is recorded at all. The chat log, which is complete at weight 1.0, holds no rider message across the driver's four messages between 08:43:00 and 08:50:45. The filer's untested assertion is the only support for the claim, against driver-side evidence of arrival, wait and contact that stands unrebutted, so the no-show the driver acted on is the only state the record shows.

No fact this case needs is left unestablished, so POL-GEN-26 does not arise and POL-NS-26 leaves the no-show ruling with the AI. The facts that decide it - arrival, the served free wait and the contact obligation - rest on EV-TRIP-00903 and EV-CHAT-00903, both complete artifacts at weight 1.0; the GPS trace (0.6; LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD) and the fare ledger (0.75; PARTIAL_RECORD) corroborate and record those facts rather than carry them alone, and I disclose their impairment rather than build the ruling on it. There is accordingly no open question for a reviewer to resolve and no ground to hold the fee.
